co_red_feather_lakes.blurb: Red Feather Lakes is a small town northwest of Fort Collins, known for its lakes and for granite domes that run on as far as you can see. Bouldering and trad are the most common climbing, and a few crags also carry bolted lines. Trad and sport routes centre on 5.10 to 5.12, with a handful of easier lines in the 5.7 to 5.9 range and a few 5.13s, while the boulder problems stay mostly in the V0 to V4 range. Grazing Allotment Crag holds the most climbs and is described as a good all-season crag. Dome with a View is a granite dome with both a sunny side and a shady side through the day, mostly trad with several pure sport lines. Boy Scout Road Areas, Lady Moon Areas and Creedmore Lakes Road hold more of the climbing.

co_redstone_area.blurb: The Redstone Area lies around the small town of Redstone, south of Carbondale on Colorado's Western Slope. Bouldering makes up most of the climbing, with sport routes next and some water ice. The boulders in the aspen woods outside town, and the River Boulders on the shore of the Crystal River, are made of the same giant red conglomerate-sandstone. Problems span V0 to V10 with plenty in the easy and moderate range, though much of the forest bouldering is aimed at advanced climbers. Sport routes run roughly 5.8 to 5.12, and the ice mostly falls in the WI4 to WI5 range. Redstone Boulders holds the most climbs, followed by River Boulders and Beginner's Luck Boulder.

mn_ely_s_peak_bouldering.blurb: Ely's Peak is a short crag inside the city limits of Duluth, Minnesota. The rock is solid basalt, with a blend of crack and face climbing. Most roped climbing is top rope, with a few good trad leads and some sport lines on Nordeast Bluff, and most of it sits below 5.11, with the best-known lines mostly between 5.6 and 5.8. Tunnel Bluff holds the most roped climbs at about 60 feet, while Northwest Bluff climbs are around 45 to 50 feet. Bouldering is a big part of the picture, with problems spread over ALC (Alternative Living Cave), Trailside Boulders, Bluff Boulder and Pine Slabs, among others, mostly in the V2 to V5 range and running up to V7, including slabs, arêtes and sit starts.

oh_marne_road.blurb: Marne Road is a roadside sandstone crag near Newark in central Ohio, mixing sport climbing and bouldering with a few trad lines. Roped routes run about 25 to 65 feet and centre on 5.11 and 5.12, with a good set of 5.9 and 5.10 lines and a few easier ones. Boulder problems run from V1 to V8, with some highballs. The terrain varies from low-angle slab to steep, powerful pocket pulling and cracks, and the rock ranges from very solid to crumbly, with loose bands. Cracks and some other spots stay wet into early summer from seepage, so winter and spring conditions can be hit or miss. Genesis Wall and East Side Boulders holds the most climbs, followed by West Side Boulders and Poison Ivy Wall (The Cave). Warm-Up Wall has mostly moderate sport routes.

qc_mont_king_3.blurb: Mont-King is a series of cliffs above Val-David in Quebec's Laurentides, in a regional park. Trad dominates, with some sport lines, a few multi-pitch routes, a bouldering area and a little ice. Grades run from easy 5.3 trad up to 5.14, with the bulk between 5.8 and 5.12, so it offers plenty for moderate leaders as well as strong ones. Sectors include Amphitheatre, Zébrée, Impériale, Vallot and Staircase, and Staircase holds the most roped climbs. Impériale faces roughly south and is fairly sunny, though trees below usually give shade at the base. Mont-King Bouldering holds the most climbs overall. It can get crowded on nice days.
